**Freezing point of water at 10 kPa**

| Pressure | Freezing (melting) point of water |
|----------|-----------------------------------|
| 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) | **≈ –20 °C** |

**Why –20 °C?**  
The melting curve of ice (solid–liquid equilibrium) follows the Clausius–Clapeyron relation. As pressure decreases below atmospheric pressure, the equilibrium temperature at which ice melts also drops. At the triple‑point pressure of 6.112 kPa (≈ 0.006 atm) the melting point is 0.01 °C. When the pressure is increased to 10 kPa, the melting point rises to roughly –20 °C. This value is consistent with experimental phase‑diagram data for water.

So, at 10 kPa, water would freeze (or melt) at about **–20 °C**.
